newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: GOLF-SWEDE JONZON DASHES OLAZABAL HOPES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SWEDE JONZON DASHES OLAZABAL HOPES.

text.p: Sweden's Michael Jonzon halted
Jose Maria Olazabal's victory hopes in his second comeback
tournament to win the Portuguese Open by three strokes at
Aroeira on Sunday.
The 24-year-old Scandinavian shot a final round 69 for a
19-under-par 269 to earn his first European tour victory in
relative comfort.
Olazabal, who had finished 12th in the Dubai Desert Classic
on his first outing after 18 months of foot trouble, had started
the day sharing second spot, two behind the tall,
powerfully-built Swede.
But despite building on his third round 65 with two early
birdies, Olazabal was unable to maintain his challenge,
finishing with a final round 74 to share fourth place with
Australians Stephen Allan and Wayne Riley, and Britain's Darren
Clarke.
Spain's Ignacio Garrido, son of former Ryder Cup golfer
Antonio, shot a closing round 65 to finish second, three clear
of Britain's Paul Broadhurst on 276.
Jonzon, producing golf of the highest calibre, collected four
birdies in his outward 32 and was able to turn for home with a
five-shot lead.
Despite losing his ball at the 10th after his drive was lost
in the woods, he escaped with a bogey six, sinking a 20 foot
putt.
Olazabal missed a golden opportunity to pick up two strokes
when he failed with a birdie putt from five feet on the same
green, put his second into a bush en route to a bogey at the
11th, and when he suffered another at the 13th, his hopes
effectively vanished.
Jonzon also dropped a shot at the 13th, but gained his fifth
birdie at the 16th to clinch the 24th European Tour title for
Sweden since Ove Sellberg gain his nation's first in 1986.
"I was surprised how calm and relaxed I was," said Jonzin
afterwards. "I was much more nervous in the third round. But I
have proved to myself that I can win and now I hope to win again
soon."
Olazabal commented: "Nothing went right for me. I pulled a
lot of tee shots and I could not hole a putt. But I have no
excuses and I am a long way ahead of where I expected to be at
this stage."
